proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(R_0=\mathbb Q[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), put \(L=J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}\), and fix \(D\in\mathfrak D\) and \(y\).  By the defining property of a reduced normal form,
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\), the right-hand side says that \(F_{D,y}\) vanishes on the real variety of \(L\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}nullstellensatz}\) over \(\mathbb R\).  There are an integer \(a\geq1\), finitely many polynomials \(q_i\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\), and an element \(h\in L\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) such that
\[
 F_{D,y}^{\,2a}+\sum_i q_i^2=h.
\]
The displayed ideal membership has a finite representation \(h=\sum_{\nu=1}^k b_\nu\ell_\nu\), where \(b_\nu\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) and \(\ell_\nu\in L\).  For each \(\nu\), the definition of saturation gives an integer \(N_\nu\geq0\) for which \(s^{N_\nu}\ell_\nu\in J_{\mathcal I}\).  Taking \(N=\max_\nu N_\nu\) therefore gives
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{\,2a}+\sum_i q_i^2\right)\in J_{\mathcal I}\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega].
\]
Write the finite rational generating set of \(J_{\mathcal I}\) as \(f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\).  There are consequently polynomials \(a_j\in\mathbb R[p_z:z\in\Omega]\) satisfying the finite coefficient identity
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{\,2a}+\sum_i q_i^2\right)
   =\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}a_jf_j. \tag{1}
\]

Fix the integers \(a,N,k,\ell\) and all monomial supports occurring in one real solution of (1).  Equating coefficients in (1) is then a finite existential sentence in the unknown coefficients of the \(q_i\) and \(a_j\), and every coefficient of that sentence is rational.  The sentence is true in \(\mathbb R\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}real\text{-}closed\text{-}field\text{-}transfer}\), it is true in the real algebraic closure \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) of \(\mathbb Q\).  Thus (1) may be chosen with all coefficients in \(\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}\).  Only finitely many coefficients occur, so they generate a finite real algebraic extension \(E/\mathbb Q\).

Identity (1) is the promised real-Nullstellensatz and saturation certificate.  Indeed, at any real point \(p\) at which every \(f_j\) vanishes and \(s(p)\neq0\), evaluation of (1) and division by \(s(p)^N\) give
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)^{2a}+\sum_iq_i(p)^2=0.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative in the selected real embedding of \(E\), hence \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  This is precisely membership in \(K_{\mathcal I}\) under the vanishing interpretation in \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\).

Finally, encode \(E\) by exact algebraic-number data for its finitely many generators, encode polynomial coefficients in an exact finite-dimensional \(\mathbb Q\)-basis, and supply every polynomial and every product in (1) in expanded form, as required in the statement.  A checker verifies the algebraic-number relations and the selected real embeddings, recomputes each advertised product by schoolbook multiplication, and compares the two expanded coefficient maps in (1).  Addition, multiplication, and equality in the supplied finite-dimensional exact representation require a number of rational operations polynomial in its expanded length; collection of like monomials is likewise polynomial because every exponent is in unary and every expanded monomial is part of the input.  Hence deterministic verification is polynomial in the total expanded certificate length.  This proves the lemma; no uniform numerical bound on the length of the shortest certificate is asserted.

Fix an input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\).  That definition makes \(\mathfrak D\) finite and nonempty.  The number of outcome cells is
\[
 n_Y=\left|\prod_{v\in Y}\Omega_v\right|
     =\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|<\infty,
\]
so there are \(|\mathfrak D|n_Y\) ordered comparisons \((D,y)\).  The finite sums, products, marginalizations, and polynomial reductions in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) construct each rational circuit \(T_{D,y}=A_{D,y}/B_{D,y}\) and each integer polynomial \(F_{D,y}\) after finitely many exact operations.

The preprocessing prescribed by \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\) computes, in the fixed order, whether
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0.
\]
This preprocessing terminates: exact real-radical membership is a first-order real-algebraic decision problem, and \(\mathrm{lem{:}tarski\text{-}effective\text{-}qe}\) supplies a terminating exact decision method.  The resulting zero normal forms require no positive-chamber feasibility call.  If every normal form is zero, \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\) gives
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p)
 \qquad
 (D\in\mathfrak D,\ y,\ p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}), \tag{2}
\]
and \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies a finite exactly checkable real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identity for every comparison.  The algorithm therefore terminates on its fast equality branch.

Suppose instead that at least one normal form is nonzero.  Acceptance of \(\mathfrak u\) certifies by exact rational arithmetic that
\[
 p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega.
\]
The finitely many values \(F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\) are decidable by exact rational arithmetic.  If one is nonzero, strict positivity of \(p^{\circ}\) makes every recorded observed-marginal denominator positive, and \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) yields
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})}
 {B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})}\neq0. \tag{3}
\]
Thus the prescribed precheck returns an exact rational, and hence real-algebraic, separator.

If the supplied table does not separate, process every nonzero-normal-form pair in canonical order.  For one such pair define
\[
 h_c(p)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal C_0(\mathcal I,c)}g(p)^2
 \qquad\{c:\mathcal I(c)=0\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm{:}rational\text{-}positive\text{-}separation}\), the existence of a table satisfying normalization, all oracle-one equalities, all strict cell inequalities, all inequalities \(h_c(p)>0\), and \(F_{D,y}(p)\neq0\) is decided after finitely many exact operations.  There is at most one such positive-chamber feasibility decision for each of the \(|\mathfrak D|n_Y\) comparisons.  If a formula is feasible, that theorem returns
\[
 p^\dagger\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb R_{\mathrm{alg}}^\Omega,
 \qquad
 T_{D,y}(p^\dagger)\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^\dagger). \tag{4}
\]
Its rational univariate representation, coordinate minimal polynomials, and isolating or Thom data permit exact checks of normalization, strict positivity, every oracle-one equality, every oracle-zero nonvanishing block, and the inequality in (4).  Because one coordinate differs, the two intervention vectors differ, and the algorithm returns the separator branch.

It remains to treat the case in which every tested positive-chamber formula is infeasible.  For each nonzero-normal-form pair, \(\mathrm{thm{:}rational\text{-}positive\text{-}separation}\) then supplies a finite quantifier-elimination trace or Positivstellensatz identity proving
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)=0
 \qquad(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}). \tag{5}
\]
For every zero-normal-form pair, \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies an identity
\[
 s^N\left(F_{D,y}^{2a}+\sum_iq_i^2\right)
 =\sum_j a_jf_j,
 \qquad J_{\mathcal I}=\langle f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\rangle. \tag{6}
\]
If \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), normalization and the oracle-one equalities make every \(f_j(p)\) zero.  Strict cell positivity makes each observed marginal occurring in a recorded denominator positive; hence \(s(p)\neq0\).  Evaluating (6), dividing by \(s(p)^N\), and using nonnegativity of even powers and squares prove \(F_{D,y}(p)=0\).  In both (5) and (6), denominator positivity and the cross-signature identity give
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)-T_{D_0,y}(p)
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p)}{B_{D,y}(p)B_{D_0,y}(p)}=0. \tag{7}
\]
Thus (7) holds for all comparisons, and the algorithm returns the reference circuit together with one finite equality or infeasibility certificate per comparison.

The branches are mutually exclusive: a separator exhibits a point at which the universal equality certificate is false.  They are exhaustive because each of the finitely many positive-chamber formulas is either feasible or infeasible.  If all represented-DAG intervention laws are common on \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), no separator formula is feasible, so the equality branch is returned.  Conversely, (7) proves commonality whenever that branch is returned.  This establishes the stated if-and-only-if assertion and the bound of at most
\[
 |\mathfrak D|\prod_{v\in Y}|\Omega_v|
\]
positive-chamber real-closed-field feasibility decisions.

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\) proves that every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) is Markov to every represented DAG.  Under the DAG intervention semantics in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), \(T_{D,y}(p)\) is the outcome-cell law after \(do(X=x)\).  Consequently the equality-branch observable circuit \(\tau(p)=(T_{D_0,y}(p))_y\) equals the common causal law \(P_x(Y)\) throughout the represented tied-sparsest family.  In the other branch the same strictly positive exact-oracle observed law supports two represented DAGs with different intervention laws, so (4) is a causal ambiguity certificate rather than merely an algebraic discrepancy.

Take \(X=\{1\}\), \(Y=\{3\}\), and \(\mathfrak G_\star=\{D_A,D_B\}\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}teh\text{-}sufficient\text{-}criterion}\), the first graphical requirement forbids a proper semidirected path from \(X\) to \(Y\) beginning with an undirected edge.  Both represented graphs are DAGs, so neither has an undirected edge and this requirement holds vacuously.

For the pairwise part of that criterion, node \(1\) is an ancestor of node \(3\) in \(D_A\), whereas it is not an ancestor of node \(3\) in \(D_B\).  Hence
\[
 A_A=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_A}(Y)=\{1\},
 \qquad
 A_B=X\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_B}(Y)=\varnothing. \tag{8}
\]
Every chain component of a DAG is a singleton.  The pertinent parent sets disagree, since
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_A}(1)=\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{pa}_{D_B}(1)=\{3,4\}. \tag{9}
\]
Thus the parent-set alternative in the cited criterion fails.  For its reweighted-graph alternative, the ancestral margin relevant to outcome node \(3\) in \(D_A\) has vertex set \(\{1,2,3\}\) and arrows \(1\to3\leftarrow2\), while (8) makes the corresponding ancestral margin in \(D_B\) the singleton graph on \(\{3\}\).  Markov equivalence requires the same vertex set, so these two reweighted ancestral graphs are not Markov equivalent.  Both pairwise alternatives fail, and therefore the sufficient criterion is not satisfied.

By \(\mathrm{prop{:}four\text{-}node\text{-}cross\text{-}mec\text{-}witness}\), the input \(\mathfrak u_\star\) is accepted, its supplied rational witness belongs to the exact-oracle model, and
\[
 p_\star\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I_\star}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^{16},
 \qquad
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)=\frac{13}{20}\neq\frac12=T_{D_B,+1}(p_\star). \tag{10}
\]
Let \(D_0\) be the first of \(D_A,D_B\) in the canonical graph order and let \(D\) be the other.  If every fixed-order normal form were zero, \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\), applied to the admitted table \(p_\star\), would force equality in (10).  Therefore at least one normal form is nonzero, so \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\) reaches its exact test of the supplied table \(p^{\circ}=p_\star\).  Equation (10) and positivity of its recorded marginal denominators imply
\[
 F_{D,+1}(p_\star)
 =B_{D,+1}(p_\star)B_{D_0,+1}(p_\star)
   \{T_{D,+1}(p_\star)-T_{D_0,+1}(p_\star)\}\neq0. \tag{11}
\]
The algorithm therefore returns \((D_0,D,p_\star)\) at that supplied-witness precheck.  Its output is rational and strictly positive, and its two graphwise causal values are exactly those in (10).  Equations (8)--(9) place this query outside the cited sufficient graphical region, while (10)--(11) give a checkable ambiguity decision.  Hence the algorithm resolves at least one tied-sparsest query on which that sufficient-only test is undecided, proving the asserted strictness in decision-output coverage.

Fix \(\mathfrak u\), its equality-branch circuit \(\tau\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\),
\[
 P_z>0\qquad(z\in\Omega). \tag{12}
\]
Every factor recorded in a denominator \(B_{D,y}\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) is an observed marginal probability, hence a nonempty sum of the cells in (12).  Therefore
\[
 B_{D,y}(P)>0\qquad(D\in\mathfrak D,\ y). \tag{13}
\]
There are finitely many such pairs.  Polynomial continuity supplies an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(P\) on which every denominator in (13) remains positive.  Each coordinate of \(\tau\) is a quotient of polynomials with nonvanishing denominator on \(U\), so \(\tau\) is continuously differentiable on \(U\), with derivative \(J_\tau\).

For each cell \(z\), let \(e_z\in\mathbb R^m\) denote its coordinate vector and define \(W_i=e_{Z_i}-P\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}multinomial}\) and the definition of \(\widehat p_n\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_PW_i=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P(W_iW_i^{\mathsf T})
 =\operatorname{diag}(P)-PP^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i. \tag{14}
\]
The \(W_i\) have finite support, so their second moments are finite.  Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}iid\text{-}clt}\) to (14) yields
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_P), \tag{15}
\]
with singular \(\Sigma_P\) allowed.  Also,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\|\widehat p_n-P\|_2^2
 =\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_P)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\widehat p_n\to P\) in probability.  Consequently
\[
 \Pr_P(\widehat p_n\in U)\longrightarrow1. \tag{16}
\]
By the construction of \(U\), (16) implies that the denominator event in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) has probability tending to one.

Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}multivariate\text{-}delta\text{-}method}\) to (15) and the differentiable map \(\tau\).  On \(U\),
\[
 \tau(P+h)=\tau(P)+J_\tau(P)h+r(h),
 \qquad
 \frac{\|r(h)\|}{\|h\|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Equation (15) gives \(\sqrt n\|\widehat p_n-P\|=O_P(1)\), and consistency plus (16) gives \(\sqrt n\,r(\widehat p_n-P)=o_P(1)\) on an event of probability tending to one.  On that event \(\widehat\tau_n=\tau(\widehat p_n)\); the off-event value in \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) is asymptotically irrelevant.  Therefore
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_n-\tau(P)\}
 =J_\tau(P)\sqrt n(\widehat p_n-P)+o_P(1)
 \Rightarrow
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}\right). \tag{17}
\]

Both maps
\[
 p\longmapsto\operatorname{diag}(p)-pp^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 p\longmapsto J_\tau(p)
\]
are continuous at \(P\), the second because the rational circuit is continuously differentiable on \(U\).  Hence
\[
 \widehat\Sigma_n\xrightarrow{P}\Sigma_P,
 \qquad
 J_\tau(\widehat p_n)\xrightarrow{P}J_\tau(P)
\]
on the event in (16).  Continuity of matrix multiplication, again using that the complement of this event has probability tending to zero, gives
\[
 \widehat V_n
 \xrightarrow{P}
 J_\tau(P)\Sigma_PJ_\tau(P)^{\mathsf T}. \tag{18}
\]

The circuit under consideration is an equality-branch circuit.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}equality\text{-}branch\text{-}soundness}\), for every \(D\in\mathfrak D\),
\[
 \tau_y(P)=T_{D,y}(P). \tag{19}
\]
The same lemma invokes the common-law Markov property, and \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) identifies the right-hand side of (19) with the DAG truncated-factorization law after \(do(X=x)\).  Thus
\[
 \tau_y(P)=P_x(Y=y), \tag{20}
\]
which proves the relationship between the observed-law circuit and the causal target rather than defining the target to be the circuit.

Finally fix the stated outcome cell and use \(\mathrm{ass{:}nondegenerate\text{-}cell}\), namely \(\sigma_y^2>0\).  The scalar marginal of (17), (18), and (20) gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\sigma_y^2),
 \qquad
 \widehat V_{n,yy}\xrightarrow{P}\sigma_y^2>0. \tag{21}
\]
The sandwich matrix is positive semidefinite on the denominator event, and (21) makes its \(y\)-diagonal entry strictly positive with probability tending to one.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}slutsky\text{-}scalar}\),
\[
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,y}-P_x(Y=y)\}}
 {\sqrt{\widehat V_{n,yy}}}
 \Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1). \tag{22}
\]
The boundary points \(-1.96\) and \(1.96\) have zero probability under the limiting law.  Hence (22) implies that the limiting coverage of the stated interval is
\[
 \Pr\{-1.96\leq Z\leq1.96\}
 =2\Phi(1.96)-1
 =0.9500042097\ldots,
 \qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
This proves all assertions.

Fix an accepted \(\mathfrak u\), a table \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), a graph \(D\in\mathfrak D\), and an outcome cell \(y\), and put \(L=J_{\mathcal I}:s^{\infty}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\), normalization and every oracle-one generator vanish at \(p\); hence
\[
 h(p)=0\qquad(h\in J_{\mathcal I}). \tag{23}
\]
The same definition gives \(p_z>0\) for every cell.  Every factor recorded in any \(B_{D',y'}\) is, by \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), a nonempty observed marginal and therefore a nonempty sum of positive cells.  Consequently
\[
 B_{D',y'}(p)>0\quad(D'\in\mathfrak D,\ y'),
 \qquad s(p)\neq0. \tag{24}
\]
If \(h\in L\), saturation gives an integer \(N\geq0\) such that \(s^Nh\in J_{\mathcal I}\).  Equations (23)--(24) imply \(s(p)^Nh(p)=0\), and division by the nonzero quantity \(s(p)^N\) gives \(h(p)=0\).  Thus \(p\) belongs to the real variety of \(L\).

The hypothesis of the lemma gives
\[
 \operatorname{NF}_{\prec,K_{\mathcal I}}(F_{D,y})=0.
\]
By the defining property of the canonical reduced basis used by the normal-form map, this is equivalent to \(F_{D,y}\in K_{\mathcal I}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}saturated\text{-}real\text{-}radical}\) identifies \(K_{\mathcal I}=\sqrt[\mathbb R]{L}\) with the rational polynomials vanishing on the real variety of \(L\).  Therefore
\[
 F_{D,y}(p)=0. \tag{25}
\]
Using \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\) and the positive denominators in (24), (25) is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{A_{D,y}(p)}{B_{D,y}(p)}
 =\frac{A_{D_0,y}(p)}{B_{D_0,y}(p)}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), this says
\[
 T_{D,y}(p)=T_{D_0,y}(p). \tag{26}
\]
The choices of \(p,D,y\) were arbitrary, so (26) holds throughout the exact-oracle model for every represented graph and outcome cell.  Moreover, \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\) makes each such \(p\) Markov to each represented DAG.  Under the truncated-factorization intervention semantics in \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), the two sides of (26) are graph-indexed causal intervention cells.  Hence \(\tau(p)=(T_{D_0,y}(p))_y\) is their common intervention law, not merely an observed regression vector.

Finally, \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}size}\) supplies, for each zero normal form, a finite real-Nullstellensatz and saturation identity over a finite real algebraic extension of \(\mathbb Q\).  Its proof shows that exact verification is polynomial in the expanded certificate length.  Thus every equality asserted by the output has the stated independently checkable certificate.

Fix an accepted input \(\mathfrak u\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), the supplied table has rational coordinates and its certificate establishes
\[
 p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega. \tag{27}
\]
All generators of the exact-oracle model, all recorded denominators, and all cross-signatures are polynomials with rational or integer coefficients.  Substitution of \(p^{\circ}\), clearing its positive coordinate denominators, and integer comparison therefore decide normalization, strict cell positivity, every oracle-one equality, every oracle-zero sum-of-squares inequality, denominator nonvanishing, and every condition \(F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq0\) after finitely many exact rational operations.  This proves termination and exactness of the supplied-witness precheck in \(\mathrm{def{:}sparse\text{-}simid}\).

If that precheck returns \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\), its return condition and (27) give some outcome cell \(y\) for which
\[
 F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq0. \tag{28}
\]
Strict positivity in (27) makes every observed marginal recorded by \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\) positive, so
\[
 B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})>0. \tag{29}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}cross\text{-}signature}\), equations (28)--(29) imply
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})-T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})
 =\frac{F_{D,y}(p^{\circ})}
 {B_{D,y}(p^{\circ})B_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ})}\neq0.
\]
One unequal coordinate makes the two represented-DAG intervention vectors differ.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}common\text{-}law\text{-}redundancy}\) and the intervention semantics of \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\text{-}functional}\), both vectors are causal intervention laws associated with the same admissible observed table.  This proves the proposed narrowed lemma.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Lemma (sound supplied rational-witness precheck).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), all membership and signature tests at the supplied table \(p^{\circ}\) in the nonzero-normal-form branch of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminate by exact rational arithmetic.  Whenever that precheck returns \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\), one has \(p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega\) and, for at least one outcome cell \(y\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ});
\]
hence the two represented-DAG intervention vectors differ.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current algorithm definition contains no bounded rational-table enumeration, so the cardinality and height assertion has no defined construction to which it can apply. The supplied rational exact-oracle table is the only rational precheck retained before semialgebraic feasibility. Restricting the lemma to that single precheck removes the obsolete search claim while preserving the exact arithmetic and separator-soundness conclusion actually used by the algorithm.

proposed.statement:
Lemma (sound supplied rational-witness precheck).  For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), all membership and signature tests at the supplied table \(p^{\circ}\) in the nonzero-normal-form branch of \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) terminate by exact rational arithmetic.  Whenever that precheck returns \((D_0,D,p^{\circ})\), one has \(p^{\circ}\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap\mathbb Q^\Omega\) and, for at least one outcome cell \(y\),
\[
 T_{D,y}(p^{\circ})\neq T_{D_0,y}(p^{\circ});
\]
hence the two represented-DAG intervention vectors differ.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim removes the undefined bounded enumeration and its certificate-bound dependency, and adds the common-law lemma used to interpret a failed signature as causal ambiguity.

proposed.statement: Corollary 1 (strictness relative to Teh--Sadeghi--Soo). For the certified input \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) and query \(P_{Y_1=+1}(Y_3=+1)\), the sufficient graphical conditions of Theorem 3.2 of Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo are not satisfied, whereas \(\operatorname{SparseSIM\text{-}ID}\) returns a rational positive separator; the table \(p_{\star}\) is an explicit admissible separator with graphwise values \(13/20\) under \(D_A\) and \(1/2\) under \(D_B\). Hence SparseSIM-ID strictly tightens that sufficient-only test on certified tied-sparsest inputs by resolving at least one query on which it is undecided.
proposed.justification: This finite corollary turns the comparator relation into an auditable strict inclusion rather than a prose promise.
proposed.gap: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo give a sufficient graphical criterion and leave necessity unresolved; this certified exact-oracle instance is outside their decided region but receives a checkable nonidentification certificate.
proposed.consumer: A regression test for Tetrad SP and causaldag or GSP can verify that an undecided graphical case is reported as exact ambiguity rather than silently selecting a graph.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is unchanged, but its proof under the current algorithm uses the supplied rational witness precheck directly. The obsolete certificate-bound and bounded-enumeration dependencies are removed, and the cross-signature definition used in the proof is declared.
